column4: The people of Ad see a cloud approaching their valleys and call it rain, but are told it is the painful punishment they hastened; this is the section's exact meeting of expected sweet water, an overhead mass, and arriving عذاب.
The next ayah identifies the apparent rain cloud as a wind that destroys everything by its Lord's command, completing the destructive arrival announced in 46:24.
أَنَّا صَبَبْنَا ٱلْمَآءَ صَبًّا states the ordinary water-action behind the section's startling use of pouring for a scourge.
ثُمَّ صُبُّوا۟ فَوْقَ رَأْسِهِ مِنْ عَذَابِ ٱلْحَمِيمِ joins pouring, from above, and punishment in one command, making explicit the section's threefold image.
إِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ كَانَتْ مِرْصَادًا names Hell itself as a watchpoint, the compulsory ambush-place through which the section hears retribution arrive.
إِنَّا لَمَّا طَغَا ٱلْمَآءُ recalls the Flood as water that transgressed its measure, exactly the section's way of hearing the tyrants' طغيان as a flood.
The opened gates of heaven release مَآءٍۢ مُّنْهَمِرٍۢ, staging punishment as a mass of water pouring down from above.
Springs are burst from the earth and the two waters meet عَلَىٰٓ أَمْرٍۢ قَدْ قُدِرَ; it joins the fecr-root's water sense to the destructive flood while retaining divine measure.
Even if the deniers saw a piece of sky falling, they would call it سَحَابٌ مَّرْكُومٌ, directly joining the misread cloud, the descending mass, and their fatal refusal to recognize it.
فَيَذَرُهَا قَاعًا صَفْصَفًا is the section's named level plain, whose صف-derived name prepares the ground for ranks.
The mountains are moved, the earth appears bare, and all are gathered without exception; this supplies the cleared ground on which the next ayah's row is formed.
وَعُرِضُوا۟ عَلَىٰ رَبِّكَ صَفًّا places the gathered people in a row before the Lord on the exposed earth of 18:47, closely matching leveling followed by ordered ranks.
The earth and mountains are lifted and crushed دَكَّةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ, a direct parallel to the doubled دك of the section's final leveling.
The Spirit and angels stand صَفًّا before the Merciful, directly matching the ranks that remain upright on the leveled ground.
The angels say وَإِنَّا لَنَحْنُ ٱلصَّآفُّونَ, identifying ordered standing in ranks as their own characteristic stance.
A rank صَفًّا is likened to بُنْيَانٌ مَّرْصُوصٌ; the ayah fuses the section's surviving row with its fallen architectural image.
ٱلَّذِى جَمَعَ مَالًا وَعَدَّدَهُ identifies the same wealth-gatherer whose horizontal heap the section sets beside raised columns.
He calculates that his wealth has made him immortal; the claim states why his amassed pile seems protective before the surah turns it into confinement.
إِنَّهَا عَلَيْهِم مُّؤْصَدَةٌ makes the Fire close over the wealth-counter, clarifying what the extended columns of 104:9 do to him.
فِى عَمَدٍۢ مُّمَدَّدَةٍۭ is the section's explicit second column scene: amassed wealth cannot save its builder from enclosure within extended columns.
A spring drunk by God's servants is made to gush by them, يُفَجِّرُونَهَا تَفْجِيرًا; it unites the fecr-root's water branch, servants, and the gardenward destination exactly as the section says.
The demanded garden of palms and vines must have rivers burst through it تَفْجِيرًا, bringing garden and the fecr-root's gushing-water sense into one scene.
Between two fruitful gardens God causes a river to burst forth, وَفَجَّرْنَا خِلَٰلَهُمَا نَهَرًا, another exact meeting of garden covering and fecr as water-opening.
Gardens of palms and grapes are paired with وَفَجَّرْنَا فِيهَا مِنَ ٱلْعُيُونِ, explicitly placing burst springs inside gardens.
فَالِقُ ٱلْإِصْبَاحِ and the night made for rest present daybreak as a splitting that ends the dark covering, the first half of the section's cover-image.
فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلَّيْلُ uses the j-n-n branch for night covering Abraham, making audible the covering sense that the section finds in جنتي.

ٱثَّاقَلْتُمْ إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ and أَرَضِيتُم بِٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا put becoming heavy toward earth and being satisfied with the nearer life in the same rebuke, the section's exact foil to the returning, mutually pleased soul.
ٱنفِرُوا۟ خِفَافًا وَثِقَالًا commands both light and heavy to set out and spend wealth and life, reversing the earthbound attachment rebuked in 9:38.

وَلَٰكِنَّهُۥٓ أَخْلَدَ إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ depicts a person clinging durably to earth and then gives an animal likeness, directly illuminating the section's wealth-lover settled like an animal that will not rise.
أَلَا بِذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ ٱلْقُلُوبُ locates true settling in remembrance, supplying the inward sense of the addressed ٱلنَّفْسُ ٱلْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ.
رَّضِىَ ٱللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا۟ عَنْهُ appears with abiding gardens, exactly expanding the section's reciprocal رَاضِيَةً مَّرْضِيَّةً and garden entry.
God is pleased with the believers and sends ٱلسَّكِينَةَ upon them beneath the tree; divine pleasure, settled calm, and living cover meet in one scene.
The disciples say the descending table will let them eat and تَطْمَئِنَّ قُلُوبُنَا; the table-image and inward tranquility meet explicitly here.

فَأَمَّا مَن طَغَىٰ opens a sequence in which transgression, preference for the nearer life, punishment, restraint of the soul, and garden are set against one another, closely recapitulating the section's arc.
وَءَاثَرَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا names preference for the lower life as the transgressor's decisive choice, corresponding to the section's earthbound satisfaction.
فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَحِيمَ هِىَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ gives the preferred lower life's destination, completing the negative half of the 79:37-41 contrast.
The opposite person fears standing before the Lord and restrains ٱلنَّفْسَ from desire; the soul now moves toward its Lord rather than settling into appetite.
فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَنَّةَ هِىَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ completes the reversal by making the garden, rather than the lower life, the soul's abiding place.
وَلَقَدْ جِئْتُمُونَا فُرَادَىٰ depicts every person arriving singly, with possessions and alleged partners left behind, exactly the solitude the section opposes to entry among God's servants.
وَكُلُّهُمْ ءَاتِيهِ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ فَرْدًا repeats the resurrection arrival as an individual, sharpening the section's pair-versus-single image.
فَذَٰلِكَ ٱلَّذِى يَدُعُّ ٱلْيَتِيمَ identifies denial by the act of pushing the orphan away, the direct opposite of coming alongside the one left alone.
وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ ٱلْمِسْكِينِ repeats beside the orphan the same failure to urge feeding that follows it in the section.
The command concerning orphans says وَإِن تُخَالِطُوهُمْ فَإِخْوَٰنُكُمْ; mixing with them as brothers directly answers the image of the orphan as a person with nobody beside him.
The command to return orphan property and not consume it into one's own wealth directly exposes the section's image of swallowing another person's share into a solitary heap.
Men and women each have نَصِيبٌ مَّفْرُوضٌ from what relatives leave; fixed shares form the legal boundary against eating an inheritance without division.
When relatives, orphans, and the poor attend the division, they are to be provided and addressed kindly, turning inheritance-sharing itself into the section's communal table.
Those who consume orphan wealth unjustly are described as eating fire into their bellies, making the hidden reality of the section's indiscriminate inheritance-eating concrete.
They feed food they love to the poor, orphan, and captive; loved provision becomes a shared table rather than a hoarded pile.
قِيلَ ٱدْخُلِ ٱلْجَنَّةَ places the faithful man inside the garden before his wish, directly paralleling the soul's invitation to enter while reversing the condemned man's belated wish.
His wish concerns his Lord's forgiveness and making him مِنَ ٱلْمُكْرَمِينَ, relocating honor from wealth to pardon and admission exactly as the section explains.
يَٰعِبَادِ لَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ addresses God's servants with reassurance at the last day, closely matching the peaceful call that gathers the soul among the servants.
The intervening ayah identifies those servants by faith and submission, specifying who receives the reassurance of 43:68 and entry of 43:70.
ٱدْخُلُوا۟ ٱلْجَنَّةَ calls those servants and their spouses into the garden together, joining entry, community, and the pair-image.
The promised person comes بِقَلْبٍ مُّنِيبٍ, a returning heart, supplying the inward return immediately before the command to enter in peace.
ٱدْخُلُوهَا بِسَلَٰمٍ is the same gardenward call with peace that the section hears addressed to the tranquil soul.
فَوَٰكِهُ وَهُم مُّكْرَمُونَ places being honored amid garden provision, opposing the claim that worldly wealth itself proves honor.
عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍۢ مُّتَقَٰبِلِينَ seats the honored people face to face, a concrete afterlife reversal of the orphan's unsupported singleness.
كُلُوا۟ وَٱشْرَبُوا۟ هَنِيٓـًٔۢا بِمَآ أَسْلَفْتُمْ turns what was sent ahead in former days into a feast, answering the futile wish that one had sent something ahead for true life.
إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتْقَىٰكُمْ states the criterion of honor before God, directly correcting the wealth-based claim of being honored.
Solomon calls the gift before him a test of whether he will give thanks, and affirms that his Lord is self-sufficient and generous; possession is thus trial rather than proof of personal honor.
وَلْتَنظُرْ نَفْسٌ مَّا قَدَّمَتْ لِغَدٍ commands every soul to inspect what it has sent ahead, directly supplying the timely counterpart to the last-day regret over failing to prepare for life.
True righteousness includes giving wealth despite loving it to orphans and the poor, reversing both attachment to wealth and refusal of the orphan's table.
هَٰذَا عَذْبٌ فُرَاتٌ names fresh sweet water with عذب, the lexical branch the section sets against the عذاب that arrived instead of rain.
The repeated هَٰذَا عَذْبٌ فُرَاتٌ contrasts drinkable sweetness with the punishment-sense carried by the nearly same letters in the cloud scene.
وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمُعْصِرَٰتِ مَآءً ثَجَّاجًا presents the hoped-for counterpart: abundant water descending from rain clouds rather than a scourge descending as punishment.
A heavy cloud is driven to dead land and sends down water that brings every fruit forth, providing the merciful cloud-outcome that Ad wrongly expected in 46:24.
Those who are رَضُوا۟ بِٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱطْمَأَنُّوا۟ بِهَا combine satisfaction and tranquility in the lower life; this is the precise false rest reversed by the soul pleased with its Lord.
بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا names the preference that makes a person settle into the lower life rather than answer the return-call.
وَٱلْءَاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ sets what is better and lasting against the lower life preferred in 87:16, clarifying the destination of the return.
God raises the heavens بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍۢ تَرَوْنَهَا; the enduring divine elevation without visible columns is a boundary to the human stone columns the section sees leveled.
The same creation claim, heavens raised بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍۢ تَرَوْنَهَا, repeats the contrast between divine support and doomed human monumental supports.
The earth is seen خَٰشِعَةً, then quivers and swells when water descends; its low stillness is not death, offering a natural counterpart to the soul lowered yet alive and responsive after upheaval.
يُصَبُّ مِن فَوْقِ رُءُوسِهِمُ ٱلْحَمِيمُ gives the section's vertical action precisely, though this ayah names poured boiling water rather than a poured scourge.
The roof falls on plotters مِن فَوْقِهِمْ and punishment reaches them from where they do not perceive; this joins collapsed construction, descent from above, and an ambush-like arrival.
Punishment covers them from above and from beneath their feet, spatially developing the section's overhead recompense at the traveler's unavoidable ground.
وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِم مَّطَرًا calls a destructive visitation rain, a specific reversal of the life-giving rain expected from a cloud.
وَٱقْعُدُوا۟ لَهُمْ كُلَّ مَرْصَدٍ uses the same r-s-d branch for literal watchers stationed at every ambush-place, clarifying the spatial force of مرصاد in the section.
The question about the mountains is answered by their being blown away, supplying the removal that produces the صفصف plain in 20:106.
The level plain has neither crookedness nor elevation, defining the exact flatness on which the section imagines the ranks standing.
وَبُسَّتِ ٱلْجِبَالُ بَسًّا stages the mountains crushed to pieces in the final upheaval, a close nonlexical parallel to the earth's repeated pounding.
The crushed mountains become scattered dust, completing the removal of upright mass begun in 56:5.
The mountains are set moving until they are a mirage; within the same surah Hell becomes مرصاد and the angels later stand in a row, so this ayah supplies the cleared terrain of that meeting.
The angels say each of them has a known station, specifying the ordered places from which they declare themselves the row-makers in 37:165.
God دَمْدَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ and سَوَّىٰهَا against Thamud; the named people, crushing punishment, and leveling meet, though the object of leveling admits more than one reading.
The wealth-counter is thrown into the Crusher, turning the confidence of 104:3 toward the enclosure by extended columns in 104:8-9.
فَٱنفَجَرَتْ مِنْهُ ٱثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ عَيْنًا uses the fecr branch for water bursting from rock and assigns each people its drinking-place, joining eruption with apportioned access.
The demand that Muhammad تَفْجُرَ لَنَا مِنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ يَنۢبُوعًا preserves the fecr-root's spring-opening sense without yet adding the garden supplied in 17:91.
وَإِذَا ٱلْبِحَارُ فُجِّرَتْ applies the fecr branch to waters bursting open at the last upheaval, the catastrophic boundary to the measured garden spring.
Water descends from heaven بِقَدَرٍ and is lodged in the earth, presenting the controlled provision against which transgressive flood and freely directed garden spring are heard.
The measured water of 23:18 produces gardens of palms and grapes, joining proportioned water to garden provision.
فِيهَا عَيْنٌ جَارِيَةٌ places a flowing spring inside the high garden, a concise parallel to the water found after the soul enters.
فِيهِمَا عَيْنَانِ تَجْرِيَانِ gives the paired gardens two flowing springs, combining the pair-image with controlled paradise water.
فِيهِمَا عَيْنَانِ نَضَّاخَتَانِ depicts two gushing springs within the paired gardens, another measured counterpart to the flood.
The retreating night supplies the covering that is being withdrawn immediately before the morning breathes in 81:18.
وَٱلصُّبْحِ إِذَا تَنَفَّسَ personifies morning emerging after retreating night, a close parallel to dawn opening the dark cover.
وَٱلَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَىٰ explicitly makes night a covering, the surface the section says dawn rends.
وَٱلنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّىٰ makes daylight's unveiling the counterpart to night covering in 92:1.
فَأَلْهَمَهَا فُجُورَهَا وَتَقْوَىٰهَا names فجور within the soul and sets it against piety, supporting the section's moral breach between fecr's opening and garden's cover.
بَلْ يُرِيدُ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ لِيَفْجُرَ أَمَامَهُ uses the fecr branch for the human wish to keep breaching ahead, the moral sense the section locates between its first and last words.
Those who prefer the lower life also obstruct God's path and seek it crooked; worldly preference is thus joined to blocking the journey the soul should make.
بَلْ تُحِبُّونَ ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ identifies love of the immediate life, close to the section's adhesive love of wealth and earth.
وَتَذَرُونَ ٱلْءَاخِرَةَ states what that immediate attachment leaves behind, defining the lost direction of travel.
Those people love ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ and leave behind a heavy day; love of what is near produces the wrong kind of heaviness in the section's journey-image.
إِنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ٱلرُّجْعَىٰ states the journey's endpoint in the same return language as the call to the tranquil soul.
إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ ٱلْمُسْتَقَرُّ locates the final place of settling with the Lord, joining journey and true rest.
رَّضِىَ ٱللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا۟ عَنْهُ follows gardens with abiding residence, another exact Quranic expansion of reciprocal pleasure.
God's pleasure with the first believers and their pleasure with Him is followed by prepared gardens, repeating the section's pleasure-to-entry relation.
رَّضِىَ ٱللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا۟ عَنْهُ is paired with gardens and membership in حِزْبُ ٱللَّهِ, connecting reciprocal pleasure to entry into a gathered company.
A town once ءَامِنَةً مُّطْمَئِنَّةً with provision from every place tastes hunger and fear after ingratitude, showing that outward ease and provision are a tested, reversible tranquility.
The disciples ask whether their Lord can send down a table from heaven; it supplies the actual table whose purpose is inward reassurance in 5:113.
The boastful owner is stripped of what he names and comes to God فَرْدًا, joining wealth's loss to the resurrection singleness described by the section.
أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيمًا فَـَٔاوَىٰ answers orphan singleness with shelter, a concrete form of drawing the unsupported person alongside.
فَأَمَّا ٱلْيَتِيمَ فَلَا تَقْهَرْ turns remembered shelter into a direct command not to overpower the orphan.
The guardians must test orphans, deliver their property at maturity, and avoid consuming it wastefully or hastily, specifying the restraint absent from the section's indiscriminate eating.
أَوْ إِطْعَٰمٌ فِى يَوْمٍۢ ذِى مَسْغَبَةٍ makes feeding during hunger the difficult liberating act, opened toward the orphan in 90:15.
يَتِيمًا ذَا مَقْرَبَةٍ makes a related orphan the first person seated at that figurative table.
أَوْ مِسْكِينًا ذَا مَتْرَبَةٍ adds the poor person lying in dust, closely echoing the section's orphan-and-poor pairing.
One cannot attain righteousness until spending from what one loves, a direct ethical reversal of clinging to beloved wealth.
The God-fearing are among gardens and springs immediately before the entry-call, supplying both destination and water.
ٱدْخُلُوهَا بِسَلَٰمٍ ءَامِنِينَ calls them into that garden setting in peace and security, close to the call heard by the tranquil soul.
The garden's keepers say فَٱدْخُلُوهَا خَٰلِدِينَ to the God-fearing brought in groups; entry here is explicitly communal rather than solitary.
The entrants praise God for giving them the land to settle wherever they wish in the garden, presenting chosen settlement after the journey rather than being stuck to the lower earth.
ٱدْخُلُوا۟ ٱلْجَنَّةَ لَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكُمْ addresses people once denied mercy and calls them into the garden without fear or grief, another restorative entry scene.
The garden is brought near to the God-fearing, setting the destination immediately before the returning heart and peaceful entry of 50:33-34.
هَٰذَا مَا تُوعَدُونَ لِكُلِّ أَوَّابٍ حَفِيظٍ identifies the recipient as one who repeatedly returns, preparing the heart's arrival in 50:33.
أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ فِى جَنَّٰتٍۢ مُّكْرَمُونَ again locates honor inside gardens, supporting the section's relocation of honor away from amassed property.
ضَيْفِ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ ٱلْمُكْرَمِينَ calls Abraham's visitors honored guests, placing ikram in the social setting of receiving people at one's table.
Abraham turns to his household and brings a roasted calf, supplying the meal through which the honored-guest relation of 51:24 becomes concrete.
The section treats جنة as tree-cover; جُنَّةً here means a shield made from oaths, a plausible same-root witness to covering, though the ayah does not depict a garden.
